Takeovers can only be be performed only if the aggressor has a takeover power which his victim is vulnerable to: If you have a Rebel world, you are vulnerable to Imperium Seat If you have an Imperium card, you are vulnerable to Rebel Alliance If you have military of +1 or more, you are vulnerable to Imperium Cloaking Technology . You cannot settle and takeover in the same action. Newly placed worlds cannot be taken over. Takeovers succeed if Military of the aggressor is greater or equal to the total Military of the victim plus the defence of the target world. Expansion Arc #3: Xeno Invasion (with Invasion) The Xenos are invading! In addition to expanding your empire, you must defend it from the Xenos. Standalone expansion played only with the base game. All Explore phases have the 'mix with hand' power. Settle is already selected in round 1. Xenos attack in round 3. After discarding down to 10 , each player gets an Invasion card with the strength of the attacking Xenos. Players with a higher military vs Xenos get higher values. To defend, military vs Xenos + defence vs Xenos must exceed (not just tie) the Invasion value. Settle powers may be used for extra military force. Greatest Contributor: most ​ contributed to the war effort. Additional game end conditions: Xenos are defeated: the combined military vs Xenos of all players matches or exceeds the Xeno repulse value. No final invasion happens. All players fail to defend twice. No player gains Greatest Admiral or Greatest Contributor. Note: Military vs Xenos: for settling worlds with Xeno, contributes to defeating Xenos, counts when determining strength for invasion cards. Defence vs Xenos: only counted when defending each round. [Rating: 1/10] The cards are way too busy with stupid little symbols that needs a cheat sheet that is like the Rosetta Stone to decipher! I am sure it would become easier to remember them after several plays, but I am not sure I want to invest the time or energy. Once you learn the game I would dread playing it with new players anyway, as I would have to watch them go through the same frustration of learning the damn thing. Also, there is no way in hell I would want to teach this thing to anyone for the same reasons.  I really don't see what all the fuss is over this. There is really nothing new here. San Ju

[Rating: 1/10] I am tired of having to mark cards or write on cards just to be able to play a game, to correct for game designers poor color choices and/or obliviousness to even common color-blindnesses. These issues make your game unplayable.  This is a one and will remain a one until there is a color blind accessable version.

[Rating: 1/10] Mundane graphics, OK game play. I can see why geeks like it because of the space theme.

[Rating: 1/10] It is a multiplayer solitaire. Your choices dont effect your gaming group at all or at least not very much.  Update 2016: Reduced down to 1. Since I played Roll for the Galaxy I do not see why I would under any circumstances play Race for the Galaxy which is essentially the same itch but just plays worse. Race ftG is a pain, while Roll ftG is fun!
